title: Scalable First-Order Interior Point Trust Region Algorithms for Linearly Constrained Optimization
summary: Computing approximate Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) points for constrained nonconvex programs is a fundamental problem in mathematical programming. Interior-point trust-region (IPTR) methods are particularly attractive for such problems because they maintain strictly feasible iterates throughout the iterative process and converge to a first-order and second-order KKT solution. Their scalability, however, is limited by the repeated computation of trust-region search directions.
